name: Barbados
description: Barbados offers expats an enviable lifestyle with year-round warm weather, stunning beaches, and a politically stable environment. It's a service-driven economy with a strong emphasis on tourism and international business, making it appealing for remote workers, retirees, and entrepreneurs.
longdescription: Expat life in Barbados is characterized by a relaxed 'island time' pace, balanced with modern conveniences and a sophisticated lifestyle. The culture is a vibrant blend of African, British, and Caribbean influences, evident in its cuisine, music, and friendly, hospitable people. English is the official language, though the local Bajan dialect is widely spoken informally. The economy is stable and service-driven, with tourism, international business, and a growing remote work community as key pillars. While imported goods can be expensive, the island provides a high quality of life with good education and healthcare options. Barbados is considered one of the safer Caribbean destinations, with a low crime rate, particularly in tourist and residential areas, though general precautions are advised.

visas.name: Barbados Welcome Stamp
visas.description: The Barbados Welcome Stamp is a special 12-month visa program for non-nationals, including remote workers, freelancers, and online business owners, to live and work remotely from Barbados. Applicants must be employed by a company or own a business registered outside Barbados and are not permitted to seek local employment or provide services to local companies.
benefits: Ability to live and work remotely in Barbados for up to 12 months.
Exemption from Barbados income tax on foreign earnings.
Freedom to travel in and out of Barbados during the visa's validity.
Option to include family members (spouses and dependents) in the application.
Access to modern infrastructure, including reliable high-speed internet and quality health services.
visas.path_to_residency_description: There is a pathway to permanent residency under Section 5(2) of the Immigration Act, Cap. 190. After residing in Barbados for at least five consecutive years on a valid visa, applicants may be eligible to apply for permanent residency.
required_documents: Valid passport (scan of bio-data page for applicant and any family members over 18).
Passport-sized photographs (for applicant and any family members over 18).
Birth certificate (for applicant and any spouse/children).
Proof of relationship for dependents (e.g., marriage or birth certificates).
Income declaration certifying expected annual income of at least USD $50,000.
Proof of valid health insurance covering the entire period of stay in Barbados.

visas.name: Barbados Retirement Visa
visas.description: The Barbados Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP) for Retired Property Owners allows eligible non-nationals who own property in Barbados to reside on the island for extended or indefinite periods. It is specifically designed for retirees demonstrating financial self-sufficiency and property ownership, providing a pathway to long-term residency in Barbados.
benefits: Long-term or indefinite residency in Barbados (indefinite for those over 60)
Ability to enter and depart Barbados freely
Path to permanent residency and eventually citizenship
No limitations on length of stay for eligible permit holders
Enjoy Barbados' high quality of life in a stable environment
visas.path_to_residency_description: The SERP grants long-term residency, which can be indefinite for retired property owners aged 60 and over. After five years of continuous legal residency in Barbados, individuals become eligible to apply for Barbadian citizenship.
required_documents: Completed Extension of Stay form (Form B)
Police Certificate of Character from any country resided in for 6 months or more after age 16
Title Deeds or Land Tax document as proof of property ownership in Barbados (property valued at US$300,000 or more)
Proof of financial resources to support self and dependents (e.g., bank statements, pension documents)
Certified copy of the bio-data page of the passport
Proof of relationship to dependents (if applicable)

extra_info:
### Visas & Notes
- Barbados Welcome Stamp: 12-month remote work visa available online
- Retirement visa available for those with passive income
- Citizens of CARICOM countries have freedom of movement

Citizenship by Descent.desc: A person born outside Barbados after November 29, 1966, can become a citizen at birth if at least one parent is a Barbadian citizen who was born in Barbados. For children born abroad to at least one Barbadian parent, citizenship may be acquired by registration. Requirements include original birth certificates of the applicant and parent(s), and passport photos. Dual citizenship is recognized.

Naturalization.desc: Citizenship by naturalization can be acquired by persons with a longstanding residence, typically requiring continuous residence for at least five years, including the last 12 months prior to applying, and for an aggregate of five out of the last seven years. Applicants must be of good character and intend to reside in Barbados. The process involves gathering civil records, proving residence and integration, and submitting an application to the competent authority. For children born abroad to a Barbadian by descent, a pathway to citizenship by registration (naturalization) exists after residing in Barbados for at least seven years.

Birthright.desc: Every person born in Barbados after November 29, 1966, automatically becomes a citizen of Barbados at the date of birth, with limited exceptions (e.g., children of foreign diplomats). This is based on the principle of *jus soli*.

Spouse and Family.desc: A foreign woman who marries a citizen of Barbados may apply for citizenship through registration. This is subject to the marriage being genuine and subsisting. Required documents typically include marriage certificates and the spouse's proof of Barbadian citizenship.

tax_advice:
*   **Personal Income Tax:** For income year 2025 onwards, personal income tax rates are 11.5% on taxable income up to BBD $50,000 and 27.5% on income above BBD $50,000. This is a reduction from the previous 12.5% and 28.5% rates. There is a basic personal allowance of BBD $25,000. Pensioners aged 60 or over receive an increased personal allowance of BBD $75,000.
*   **Corporate Tax:** The standard corporate income tax rate is 5.5% for taxable income up to BBD $1,000,000. Other rates apply for higher income brackets or specific company types, with a top rate of 1% for income exceeding BBD $30,000,000. Barbados has implemented a Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax (QDMTT) to achieve a global minimum effective tax rate of 15% for qualifying multinational enterprise (MNE) groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more, effective January 1, 2024.
*   **Value Added Tax (VAT):** The standard VAT rate is 17.5% on most goods and services. Effective July 1, 2026, the VAT rate on eligible car rentals will be reduced from 17.5% to 10%. From October 1, 2026, the VAT registration threshold for small businesses will increase from BBD $200,000 to BBD $350,000. Certain supplies, such as exports and basic food items, are zero-rated. A concessionary rate of 10% applies to hotel accommodation and certain tourism-related goods and services.
*   **Capital Gains Tax:** Barbados has no capital gains tax.
*   **Welcome Stamp Visa:** Holders of the Welcome Stamp visa (for remote workers and retirees with annual income of $50,000+) are not considered tax residents and are not taxed on foreign income.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Barbados is considered a high-cost Caribbean island. A single expat typically needs USD $2,000–$4,000 per month, excluding rent. Housing, groceries (especially imported goods), and utilities are major expenses.
*   **Language:** English is the official language. While Bajan, an English-based creole, is widely spoken, standard English is used in formal settings, media, and business.
*   **Safety:** Barbados has a low crime rate, particularly in tourist and residential areas, and is generally considered safe. However, common precautions against petty crime like opportunistic theft are advised. Avoid isolated beaches at night and keep valuables out of sight.
*   **Registration:** For long-term stays, a Special Entry Permit (SEP) or the Barbados Welcome Stamp (for remote workers) are options. Health insurance coverage is mandatory for residency applications.
*   **Pace of Life:** Be prepared for a slower, more relaxed pace of life, often referred to as 'island time.' Patience is key when dealing with services and schedules.
*   **Cultural Integration:** Barbadians are known for their friendliness and hospitality. Integrating into the local community can happen through respectful engagement, supporting local businesses, and joining clubs or community events.
